claims.text: Sarvottam Cables reported Q1 revenue from operations rose to ₹1,428 crore, a 35% increase from the year-ago period
Net profit rose about 6% to ₹82 crore in Q1
Operating margins contracted by 170 basis points to 11.2% in Q1
Copper prices rose nearly 14% during the quarter
An unnamed Mumbai-based analyst stated the volume story is intact, but investors will watch whether the company can pass on higher copper costs
Shares of the company fell 3.2% to ₹1,012 on the NSE on Friday following the results
Management is maintaining full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15 to 17 percent
The Bharuch facility will contribute to revenue from the second half of FY27
Data-centre cables account for about 9 percent of domestic revenue
Management expects the share of data-centre cables in domestic revenue can double in two years
Management stated that margin contraction was mostly due to copper costs
About two-thirds of contracts have price-variation clauses that reset with a lag of one to two quarters
Management stated they are not seeing irrational pricing from competitors
Receivable days increased from 78 to 96 over the last year
The increase in receivable days is mainly due to two large state utility customers where payments are slower
The company has not observed any customer defaults
Total capex for Bharuch is ₹620 crore
About 70 percent of Bharuch capex has already been spent
Bharuch capex is funded mainly through internal accruals and some term debt
Net debt to equity is 0.35 times
Revenue from operations was ₹1,248 crore in Q1 FY27 compared to ₹1,058 crore in Q1 FY26
EBITDA was ₹140 crore in Q1 FY27 compared to ₹136 crore in Q1 FY26
EBITDA margin was 11.2% in Q1 FY27 compared to 12.9% in Q1 FY26
Profit after tax was ₹82 crore in Q1 FY27 compared to ₹77 crore in Q1 FY26
Order book stood at ₹3,900 crore as of 30 June 2026, compared to ₹3,150 crore a year ago
Exports contributed 21% of revenue in Q1 FY27 compared to 16% in Q1 FY26
The Bharuch plant will add about 30% to cable capacity
The Bharuch plant is on track to begin commercial production in Q3 FY27
Management expects to pass on higher copper prices to customers over the next two quarters
Promoter pledged holding rose to 35% from 22% six months prior as reported in March 2024
The company received a GST demand order of ₹46.3 crore including interest and penalty relating to ITC for FY2020-21 and FY2021-22
The company believes it has a strong case on merits based on legal advice and intends to file an appeal against the GST order
The company does not expect any material impact from the GST demand on its financial position or operations
Promoter & promoter group shareholding was 58.2% in Jun 2026, 58.2% in Mar 2026, and 58.4% in Jun 2025
Pledged promoter holding as a percentage of total promoter holding was 4.1% in Jun 2026, 6.0% in Mar 2026, and 11.5% in Jun 2025
FII shareholding was 11.8% in Jun 2026, 10.9% in Mar 2026, and 9.2% in Jun 2025
DII shareholding was 14.6% in Jun 2026, 14.1% in Mar 2026, and 12.7% in Jun 2025
Public and others shareholding was 15.4% in Jun 2026, 16.8% in Mar 2026, and 19.7% in Jun 2025
